subpillars.name: Reform Leadership, Coalitions and Civic Engagement

families.definition: Barriers that exclude people because of the group they belong to: discrimination, norms, missing documents, disability-related access and unequal voice.
families.core_variables: gaps in employment, earnings and access by group; representation; documentation coverage
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about gender equality, social inclusion, disability, care burdens, legal identity and digital divides by group.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes violence and coercion (Violence, coercion and exploitation) and group conflict (Horizontal inequality and social cohesion).
families.literature: Becker 1957; Phelps 1972; Bertrand and Mullainathan 2004; Chattopadhyay and Duflo 2004; Duflo 2012; Jayachandran 2015; Mitra, Posarac and Vick 2013
families.primary_reason: The Tackling Structural Exclusion definition names exactly these groups and barriers.
families.secondary_rhdr: Enhancing Capabilities: access to services is also capability | Growth through Inclusion: female labour supply raises growth
families.risks: Demographic Shifts | Growing Populism | Increased Polarisation | Technological Change

families.definition: Violence and exploitation inside households and labour markets, and the bargaining, poverty and norm channels that produce them.
families.core_variables: prevalence of IPV, child marriage, child labour; outcomes of children exposed to abuse
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about gender-based violence, child protection, child labour and social services for the vulnerable.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes crime in public space (Crime, violence and personal security).
families.literature: Basu and Van 1998; Edmonds 2007; Field and Ambrus 2008; Aizer 2010; Currie and Widom 2010
families.primary_reason: The victims are the groups the Tackling Structural Exclusion definition names, and the harm is exclusion from capability.
families.secondary_rhdr: Enhancing Capabilities: child protection is a capability investment
families.risks: Demographic Shifts | Pandemics

families.definition: How inequality between groups, polarisation and identity turn into grievance, distrust and conflict, and how contact, recognition and reconciliation reverse them.
families.core_variables: between-group inequality; polarisation indices; trust across groups; conflict events
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about social cohesion, peacebuilding, reconciliation, conflict prevention, civic and national values and minority identity.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes crime and policing (Crime, violence and personal security) and participation in decisions (Participation and community voice).
families.literature: Allport 1954; Esteban and Ray 1994; Collier and Hoeffler 2004; Miguel 2004; Stewart 2008; Cederman, Weidmann and Gleditsch 2011; Iyengar et al. 2019; Mousa 2020
families.primary_reason: Horizontal inequality is structural exclusion of groups; the plan's polarisation row files cohesion and identity here.
families.secondary_rhdr: Reform Leadership, Coalitions and Civic Engagement: participatory governance and dialogue across groups
families.risks: Increased Polarisation | Growing Populism | Democratic Backsliding | Climate Change

families.definition: Displacement by conflict, disaster, climate or projects, the impoverishment risks it creates, and integration in host communities.
families.core_variables: displaced population; host labour-market outcomes; resettlement outcomes
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about refugees, returnees, displaced people, compensation and resettlement.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes voluntary labour migration (Labour mobility and remittances).
families.literature: Cernea 1997; Black et al. 2011; Becker and Ferrara 2019
families.primary_reason: Displaced people are a marginalised community with structural barriers to access.
families.secondary_rhdr: Future Generations: planned relocation from climate-unviable places
families.risks: Climate Change | Increased Polarisation | Demographic Shifts

families.family: Household risk protection and consumption stability
families.definition: Transfers and insurance that hold household consumption and assets steady when income falls, and the risk-taking that credible protection allows.
families.core_variables: consumption volatility; coverage of shocks; distress asset sales; catastrophic spending
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about social protection coverage and systems, social assistance and insurance, pensions, unemployment and health-cost protection, targeting.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes transfers designed to lift a poverty trap (Escape from poverty traps) and emergency relief operations (Crisis response capacity).
families.literature: Townsend 1994; Holzmann and Jorgensen 2001; Gertler and Gruber 2002; Hoddinott 2006; Barr and Diamond 2008; Karlan et al. 2014; Bowen et al. 2020
families.primary_reason: Social protection is named in the Enhancing Capabilities definition; the channel is resilient lives.
families.secondary_rhdr: Tackling Structural Exclusion: coverage gaps fall on informal and excluded workers | Anticipation and Strategic Foresight: shock-responsive design is ex ante preparation | Future Generations: pension financing is intergenerational
families.risks: Pandemics | Climate Change | Shifts in Globalisation | Demographic Shifts | Growing Populism

families.definition: Transfers of cash or assets large or conditional enough to move households past thresholds that keep them poor.
families.core_variables: asset holdings; consumption levels after transfers; local multipliers
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about poverty reduction programmes, economic inclusion, graduation and household livelihoods.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes insurance against shocks (Household risk protection).
families.literature: Schultz 2004; Fiszbein and Schady 2009; Banerjee et al. 2015 (Science); Haushofer and Shapiro 2016; Bandiera et al. 2017; Egger et al. 2022
families.primary_reason: The channel is capability to escape deprivation; livelihoods are named in the Enhancing Capabilities definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Growth through Inclusion: where the asset is a productive enterprise | Tackling Structural Exclusion: ultra-poor are often excluded groups
families.risks: Growing Populism | Climate Change

families.definition: Formation of job-relevant skills after or alongside schooling, and the signals and employer links that make them pay.
families.core_variables: returns to training; skill mismatch; apprenticeship completion; digital skill levels
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about workforce skills, TVET, apprenticeships, qualifications, digital skills and lifelong learning.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes schooling (Human capital formation through schooling) and job matching (Labour market matching and regulation).
families.literature: Spence 1973; Ryan 2001; Goldin and Katz 2008; Attanasio, Kugler and Meghir 2011; Akerman, Gaarder and Mogstad 2015; Jensen 2010
families.primary_reason: Skills are named in the Enhancing Capabilities definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Growth through Inclusion: skills raise earnings of excluded workers | Export-led: skills for traded sectors
families.risks: Technological Change | Demographic Shifts | Shifts in Globalisation

families.definition: Accumulation of knowledge and skills through early childhood, school and university, and the access, quality and incentive conditions that govern it.
families.core_variables: enrolment and completion; learning outcomes; teacher effort; early-childhood development
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about access to education, quality, teachers, curriculum, early childhood, higher education and student finance.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes work-based and vocational skills (Skills formation for work).
families.literature: Becker 1964; Duflo 2001; Heckman 2006; Hanushek and Woessmann 2008; Muralidharan and Sundararaman 2011; Banerjee et al. 2017; Valero and Van Reenen 2019
families.primary_reason: Education is named first in the Enhancing Capabilities definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Tackling Structural Exclusion: access for girls, disabled and minority learners | Future Generations: early childhood is the highest-return intergenerational investment
families.risks: Demographic Shifts | Technological Change

families.definition: Coverage, quality and inputs of health services (workforce, medicines, facilities, primary care) and their effect on survival and productive health.
families.core_variables: service coverage; avoidable mortality; provider quality; workforce density; medicine availability
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about access to health services, primary care, workforce, quality, medicines and maternal and child services.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes risk factors and prevention (Disease and injury prevention) and financial protection (Household risk protection).
families.literature: Grossman 1972; Anand and Barnighausen 2004; Starfield, Shi and Macinko 2005; Das, Hammer and Leonard 2008; Bhutta et al. 2014; Wirtz et al. 2017; Kruk et al. 2018
families.primary_reason: Health is named in the Enhancing Capabilities definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Tackling Structural Exclusion: disability and remote-area access | Agility and Delivery Capability: surge capacity in emergencies
families.risks: Pandemics | Demographic Shifts

families.definition: Behavioural, infectious and injury risks to health, and the externalities and habits that make prevention under-supplied.
families.core_variables: risk-factor prevalence; infectious disease incidence; injury deaths; mental health burden
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about preventive health, communicable and non-communicable disease, substance misuse, mental health, road and transport safety, physical activity.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes service supply (Health service coverage and quality) and pollution exposure (Pollution, waste and environmental behaviour).
families.literature: Becker and Murphy 1988; Chaloupka and Warner 2000; Gersovitz and Hammer 2004; Miguel and Kremer 2004; Dupas 2011; Habyarimana and Jack 2011; Ridley et al. 2020
families.primary_reason: Healthy lives are named in the Enhancing Capabilities definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Anticipation and Strategic Foresight: infectious disease control overlaps preparedness
families.risks: Pandemics | Demographic Shifts | Environmental Degradation and Pollution

families.definition: Household command over adequate, safe food and the nutritional outcomes that follow, especially early in life.
families.core_variables: prevalence of undernourishment and stunting; food price pass-through; foodborne illness; post-harvest loss
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about food security, nutrition, school meals, food assistance, food safety and food loss.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes farm output (Primary-sector productivity growth) and price buffers against external shocks (External balance and shock absorption).
families.literature: Sen 1981; Deaton 1989; Hoddinott et al. 2008; Victora et al. 2008; Ivanic and Martin 2008; Alderman and Bundy 2012; Havelaar et al. 2015
families.primary_reason: Food security is named in the Enhancing Capabilities definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Growth through Inclusion: where the binding constraint is producer income
families.risks: Resource and Energy Pressures | Climate Change | Pandemics | Shifts in Globalisation

families.definition: Household capability gains from first access to electricity, water, sanitation, clean cooking and adequate housing.
families.core_variables: access rates; time use; diarrhoeal and respiratory disease; housing quality
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about electricity access, water and sanitation services, clean cooking, housing quality and basic infrastructure access.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes utility supply performance (Network utility performance).
families.literature: Cutler and Miller 2005; Cattaneo et al. 2009; Dinkelman 2011; Duflo et al. 2015; Hanna, Duflo and Greenstone 2016; Lee, Miguel and Wolfram 2020
families.primary_reason: Basic services are named in the Enhancing Capabilities definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Tackling Structural Exclusion: unserved households are disproportionately excluded groups | Domestic Integration: networks connect places
families.risks: Resource and Energy Pressures | Environmental Degradation and Pollution | Climate Change

families.definition: Crime and violence in public life, and the deterrence, prevention, justice and rehabilitation channels that reduce them.
families.core_variables: victimisation; homicide; clearance and recidivism rates; access to dispute resolution
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about policing, crime prevention, justice services, legal aid, corrections, organised crime and victims.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes violence inside households (Violence, coercion and exploitation) and group conflict (Horizontal inequality and social cohesion); defence and border security are Standard Governance.
families.literature: Becker 1968; Dell 2015; Chalfin and McCrary 2017; Blattman, Jamison and Sheridan 2017; Heller et al. 2017; Bhuller et al. 2020; Blattman, Hartman and Blair 2014
families.primary_reason: The Enhancing Capabilities definition is broad enough to include human security.
families.secondary_rhdr: Adaptability and Course Correction: judicial independence sits with institutional checks (F44)
families.risks: Increased Polarisation | Democratic Backsliding

families.definition: Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions as a global public good, through prices, directed innovation, cost declines and avoided lock-in.
families.core_variables: emissions intensity; carbon price; clean technology costs; share of long-lived high-carbon capital
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about renewables, low-carbon transitions, GHG targets, carbon markets, efficiency and low-emission transport and buildings.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes local pollutants (Pollution, waste and environmental behaviour) and forest carbon (Natural capital stewardship).
families.literature: Pigou 1920; Unruh 2000; Nordhaus 2008; Acemoglu et al. 2012; Allcott and Greenstone 2012; Nordhaus 2015; Way et al. 2022
families.primary_reason: Mitigation protects long-term well-being and avoids shifting costs onto future generations.
families.secondary_rhdr: Domestic Integration: energy supply composition | Export-led: green industry as a traded sector
families.risks: Climate Change | Resource and Energy Pressures

families.definition: Use and protection of ecosystems, wild stocks and land as assets with a shadow price, under common-pool and incentive problems.
families.core_variables: stock levels; habitat extent and condition; deforestation; degraded land
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about biodiversity, protected areas, forests, fisheries management, ecosystems, restoration and nature-based livelihoods.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes hazard buffering by ecosystems where framed as protection (Climate hazard exposure and adaptation).
families.literature: Gordon 1954; Ostrom 1990; Andam et al. 2008; Costello, Gaines and Lynham 2008; Burgess et al. 2012; Jayachandran et al. 2017; Dasgupta 2021
families.primary_reason: Nature and biodiversity are named in the Future Generations definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Growth through Inclusion: nature-based incomes | Export-led: nature-based tourism
families.risks: Biodiversity Loss | Climate Change | Resource and Energy Pressures | Environmental Degradation and Pollution

families.definition: Local pollution and waste as externalities, their effects on health and human capital, and the standards, prices, technique and norms that reduce them.
families.core_variables: pollutant concentrations; waste collected and recycled; exposure of children; compliance
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about pollution control, air and water quality, waste, circularity, chemicals, cleaner production and environmental awareness.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes greenhouse gases (Emissions mitigation) and enforcement capacity as such (Regulatory enforcement capacity).
families.literature: Grossman and Krueger 1995; Chay and Greenstone 2003; Copeland and Taylor 2004; Stern 2004; Allcott 2011; Greenstone and Hanna 2014; Ebenstein et al. 2017; Kaza et al. 2018
families.primary_reason: Pollution shifts costs onto future health and human capital, the Future Generations channel.
families.secondary_rhdr: Enhancing Capabilities: environmental health | Agility and Delivery Capability: enforcement capacity
families.risks: Environmental Degradation and Pollution | Climate Change

families.definition: Losses from climate hazards as a product of exposure, asset vulnerability and coping, and the location, protection and practice changes that reduce them.
families.core_variables: assets and people exposed; losses relative to assets; adaptive practice uptake
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about climate resilience and adaptation, disaster risk reduction, flood risk, resilient infrastructure and resilient cities.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes early warning and preparedness (Hazard anticipation) and post-event response (Crisis response capacity).
families.literature: Kahn 2005; Das and Vincent 2009; Burke and Emerick 2016; Hallegatte et al. 2017; Hallegatte, Rentschler and Rozenberg 2019; Kocornik-Mina et al. 2020
families.primary_reason: Climate resilience is named in the Future Generations definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Enhancing Capabilities: coping capacity of the poor | Anticipation and Strategic Foresight: risk-informed planning
families.risks: Climate Change | Biodiversity Loss

families.definition: Extraction of exhaustible resources and what happens to the rents: reinvestment, Dutch disease, volatility and rent-seeking.
families.core_variables: resource rents; genuine savings; real exchange rate; revenue volatility
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about mining and hydrocarbons, their governance and the use of their revenues.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes downstream processing (Domestic linkages) and fiscal rules in general (Fiscal sustainability across generations).
families.literature: Hartwick 1977; Corden and Neary 1982; Sachs and Warner 1995; Mehlum, Moene and Torvik 2006; van der Ploeg and Poelhekke 2009; van der Ploeg 2011
families.primary_reason: Sustainable resource use and responsible public finance are named in the Future Generations definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Domestic Integration: local content and linkages | Export-led: commodities as exports
families.risks: Resource and Energy Pressures | Shifts in Globalisation

families.definition: Whether public debt and fiscal policy can be sustained without shifting burdens onto future taxpayers, and the rules and liabilities that decide it.
families.core_variables: debt to GDP; primary balance reaction; contingent liabilities; procyclicality
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about fiscal sustainability, fiscal discipline, fiscal risk and fiscal governance.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes external-debt amplification of shocks (External balance and shock absorption).
families.literature: Auerbach, Gokhale and Kotlikoff 1991; Bohn 1998; Kaminsky, Reinhart and Vegh 2004; Reinhart, Reinhart and Rogoff 2012; Frankel, Vegh and Vuletin 2013; Bova et al. 2016
families.primary_reason: Responsible public finance and intergenerational equity are named in the Future Generations definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Agility and Delivery Capability: budget execution and expenditure control
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation | Demographic Shifts

families.family: Population age structure and lifecycle resources
families.definition: How fertility, ageing and lifecycle behaviour change labour input, saving and care needs across generations.
families.core_variables: fertility; dependency ratios; old-age participation; lifecycle saving; care demand
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about population policy, reproductive health and family planning, elderly care and older workers.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes pensions as income protection (Household risk protection) and female labour barriers (Group-based barriers).
families.literature: Becker and Lewis 1973; Bloom and Williamson 1998; Gruber and Wise 1999; Bloom et al. 2009; Lee and Mason 2010; Miller 2010; Colombo et al. 2011; Canning and Schultz 2012
families.primary_reason: Intergenerational equity is the Future Generations definition; the age-structure identity organises the note but is not a node.
families.secondary_rhdr: Enhancing Capabilities: reproductive health is a health capability | Growth through Inclusion: participation of older workers
families.risks: Demographic Shifts

families.definition: Allocation of scarce, variable and shared water among users, under pricing, storage and common-pool problems.
families.core_variables: water stress; groundwater depletion; storage per capita; allocation conflicts
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about water resources management, storage, efficiency, water security and basin cooperation.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes household water services (Access to basic services) and utility finances (Network utility performance).
families.literature: Wolf 1998; Brown and Lall 2006; Olmstead 2010; Ryan and Sudarshan 2022
families.primary_reason: Sustainable resource use is named in the Future Generations definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Anticipation and Strategic Foresight: drought and scarcity planning
families.risks: Resource and Energy Pressures | Climate Change

families.definition: Growth in the set of goods and services an economy can produce competitively, through learning, related diversification and reallocation toward higher-productivity activities.
families.core_variables: export complexity; sectoral productivity gaps; share of manufacturing and modern services
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives that seek new or upgraded products, sectors or export baskets.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes lowering the cost of reaching markets (Trade costs and market connectivity) and firm-level management and finance (Firm capability and growth).
families.literature: Hausmann, Hwang and Rodrik 2007; Hidalgo and Hausmann 2009; McMillan and Rodrik 2011; Rodrik 2016; Juhasz 2018
families.primary_reason: The dominant welfare channel runs through productivity growth in traded sectors, which is the Export-led definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Domestic Integration: where upgrading runs through domestic linkages rather than exports | Growth through Inclusion: where structural change moves workers out of low-productivity informal work
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation | Technological Change

families.definition: The fixed, variable and time costs of moving goods and services across borders, and how they decide which firms trade and how much.
families.core_variables: border time; freight and port costs; logistics performance; export entry rates
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about customs, ports, logistics, standards for export entry, air links and cross-border corridors.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes costs of moving goods inside the country (Internal market connectivity) and negotiated access to foreign markets (Market access and integration).
families.literature: Melitz 2003; Anderson and van Wincoop 2004; Djankov, Freund and Pham 2010; Hummels and Schaur 2013; Campante and Yanagizawa-Drott 2018
families.primary_reason: Trade costs determine participation in external markets, which is the Export-led channel.
families.secondary_rhdr: Domestic Integration: corridors and logistics also lower internal costs
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation

families.definition: The terms on which an economy's goods and services enter foreign markets, set by agreements, blocs, preferences and its own openness.
families.core_variables: tariff and non-tariff barriers faced and imposed; preference margins; regional trade shares
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about trade agreements, regional integration, liberalisation, preferences and economic diplomacy.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes the physical and administrative cost of trading (Trade costs and market connectivity).
families.literature: Viner 1950; Baier and Bergstrand 2007; Frazer and Van Biesebroeck 2010; Pavcnik 2002; Topalova and Khandelwal 2011
families.primary_reason: Market access governs the external demand an economy can reach.
families.secondary_rhdr: Anticipation and Strategic Foresight: LDC graduation and preference erosion are foreseeable external shocks
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation

families.definition: Inflows of foreign capital, know-how and production networks, and the conditions under which they raise domestic productivity.
families.core_variables: FDI stock and composition; supplier linkages; GVC participation
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about attracting investment, the investment climate and joining value chains.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes domestic credit markets (Credit, savings and financial access) and long-horizon public infrastructure finance (Public expenditure quality).
families.literature: Borensztein, De Gregorio and Lee 1998; Javorcik 2004; Harding and Javorcik 2011; World Bank 2020 (WDR, Trading for Development in the Age of GVCs); Baldwin 2016
families.primary_reason: The channel is foreign capital and knowledge entering traded sectors; FDI is named in the Export-led definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Domestic Integration: spillovers run through domestic supplier linkages
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation | Technological Change

families.definition: Foreign visitor spending as a services export consumed on site, and its local spillovers, capacity limits and exposure to shocks.
families.core_variables: arrivals and receipts; destination capacity; volatility of tourism demand
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about tourism development, products, destinations, quality, access and recovery.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes nature conservation that tourism depends on (Natural capital stewardship) and heritage custody (Standard People).
families.literature: Butler 1980; Faber and Gaubert 2019; Neumayer 2010; Gossling, Scott and Hall 2021
families.primary_reason: International tourism is named in the Export-led definition; its welfare channel is foreign demand.
families.secondary_rhdr: Future Generations: where the plan frames tourism around carrying capacity and nature
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation | Pandemics | Climate Change | Biodiversity Loss

families.definition: The creation, appropriation and adoption of knowledge, and the absorptive capacity that decides whether frontier technology reaches firms.
families.core_variables: R&D intensity; adoption lags; patents; researchers per capita
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about research, science, technology transfer, adoption, IP and frontier technology programmes.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes skills for using technology (Skills formation for work) and the regulation of digital risk (Regulatory updating for technological change).
families.literature: Arrow 1962; Romer 1990; Aghion and Howitt 1992; Cohen and Levinthal 1990; Comin and Hobijn 2010; Comin and Mestieri 2018; Cirera and Maloney 2017
families.primary_reason: The Export-led definition names innovation and technology upgrading that make traded sectors competitive.
families.secondary_rhdr: Enhancing Capabilities: research capacity in universities is also human capital | Anticipation and Strategic Foresight: frontier programmes are bets on future technology
families.risks: Technological Change | Shifts in Globalisation | Pandemics

families.definition: The cost of moving goods, people and information within the country, and how lowering it integrates regions into one market.
families.core_variables: internal transport costs; market access of places; price dispersion across markets
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about roads, rail, inland waterways, national infrastructure, rural access, e-commerce reach and market information.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes cross-border trade costs (Trade costs and market connectivity) and city-scale congestion (Urban agglomeration and land use).
families.literature: Jensen 2007; Donaldson 2018; Donaldson and Hornbeck 2016; Faber 2014; Asher and Novosad 2020; Aschauer 1989
families.primary_reason: The channel is integration of domestic markets and regions, the Domestic Integration definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Tackling Structural Exclusion: rural and remote access reaches excluded places | Standard Economy: maintenance of existing networks is BAU on the response scale
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation | Technological Change | Growing Populism

families.definition: The productivity gains of density and the congestion, land and housing costs that limit them, as shaped by planning and regulation.
families.core_variables: urban density; commuting time; land and housing prices; planned urban extension
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about urban planning, land-use regulation, urban mobility, new towns and city competitiveness.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes household access to services in cities (Access to basic services) and municipal governance (Decentralised provision).
families.literature: Duranton and Puga 2004; Duranton and Turner 2011; Glaeser and Gyourko 2018; Bertaud 2018; Lall, Henderson and Venables 2017
families.primary_reason: Cities are where domestic markets integrate; the welfare channel is agglomeration.
families.secondary_rhdr: Enhancing Capabilities: liveability and housing are capabilities | Future Generations: urban form locks in emissions
families.risks: Demographic Shifts | Climate Change | Environmental Degradation and Pollution

families.definition: The reliability, pricing, cost recovery and market structure of network utilities (power, gas, water, transport networks) as inputs to every domestic activity.
families.core_variables: outage frequency; cost-recovery ratio; technical and commercial losses; tariff-cost gap
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about grids, generation, utility finances, tariffs and subsidies, liberalisation and interconnection.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes household gains from first access (Access to basic services) and decarbonisation of supply (Emissions mitigation).
families.literature: Laffont and Tirole 1993; Joskow 2008; Allcott, Collard-Wexler and O'Connell 2016; Burgess, Greenstone, Ryan and Sudarshan 2020; Coady et al. 2019
families.primary_reason: Utility services are intermediate inputs that integrate domestic production; their failure is a binding constraint on firms.
families.secondary_rhdr: Future Generations: pricing and losses shape energy demand and emissions | Anticipation and Strategic Foresight: security of supply is covered in F39 where framed as insurance
families.risks: Resource and Energy Pressures | Climate Change

families.family: Domestic linkages and agglomeration of production
families.definition: Backward and forward links between firms and sectors, and the clustering that lets suppliers, buyers and workers find each other.
families.core_variables: domestic value added in output; supplier density; cluster employment
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about value chains, agro-processing, value addition, industrial zones and clusters, local content.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes upgrading into new export products (Productive capability accumulation) and smallholder access to buyers (Market participation of small producers).
families.literature: Hirschman 1958; Rodriguez-Clare 1996; Duranton and Puga 2004; Greenstone, Hornbeck and Moretti 2010; Farole and Akinci 2011; Morris, Kaplinsky and Kaplan 2012
families.primary_reason: Linkages and clusters are named in the Domestic Integration definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Export-led: where linkages are to foreign investors or export chains
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation | Resource and Energy Pressures

families.definition: The transaction costs that keep smallholders and small firms out of markets, and the collective and contractual arrangements that lower them.
families.core_variables: share of output sold; farmgate price margins; membership of producer organisations
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about farmer market access, cooperatives, producer organisations and contract arrangements.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes physical connectivity (Internal market connectivity) and processing linkages (Domestic linkages).
families.literature: de Janvry, Fafchamps and Sadoulet 1991; Barrett 2008; Bernard and Spielman 2009; Bellemare 2012
families.primary_reason: The channel is income for small producers left out of markets, the Growth through Inclusion definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Domestic Integration: participation integrates rural and urban markets
families.risks: Shifts in Globalisation | Growing Populism

families.definition: Output per unit of land, labour and inputs in farming, livestock and fisheries, and the adoption, learning and allocation frictions that hold it down.
families.core_variables: yields; input use; adoption rates; farm size distribution; losses to pests
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about agricultural production, productivity, modernisation, irrigation, inputs, extension, research and livestock.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes harvest rules for wild stocks (Natural capital stewardship) and food access by households (Food and nutrition security).
families.literature: Schultz 1964; Foster and Rosenzweig 1995; Evenson and Gollin 2003; Duflo, Kremer and Robinson 2011; Gollin, Lagakos and Waugh 2014; Christiaensen, Demery and Kuhl 2011
families.primary_reason: Agricultural growth reduces poverty more per point than non-agricultural growth (Christiaensen, Demery and Kuhl 2011), so the dominant welfare channel is income for rural households.
families.secondary_rhdr: Domestic Integration: productivity feeds agro-processing linkages | Future Generations: where practices are adapted to climate or soil
families.risks: Resource and Energy Pressures | Climate Change | Shifts in Globalisation

families.definition: The management, capital and entrepreneurial constraints that keep small firms small, and the allocation of resources across firms.
families.core_variables: firm size distribution; returns to capital; management scores; dispersion of marginal products
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about MSME support, entrepreneurship, start-ups and enterprise development.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes the rules firms operate under (Market institutions and competition) and credit markets (Credit, savings and financial access).
families.literature: de Mel, McKenzie and Woodruff 2008; Hsieh and Klenow 2009; Bloom et al. 2013; Hsieh and Olken 2014; McKenzie 2017; Bruhn, Karlan and Schoar 2018
families.primary_reason: Enterprise development and MSMEs are named in the Growth through Inclusion definition.
families.secondary_rhdr: Export-led: where firm upgrading targets export markets
families.risks: Technological Change | Shifts in Globalisation

families.definition: The rules of entry, competition, contract enforcement and state ownership that decide whether markets allocate resources to productive firms.
families.core_variables: entry costs; markups; contract enforcement time; SOE share of output
families.inclusion_rule: Objectives about the business environment, competition, consumer protection, SOEs, commercial courts and market rules.
families.exclusion_rule: Excludes firm-level support (Firm capability and growth) and regulation of digital markets (Regulatory updating for technological change).
families.literature: Djankov et al. 2002; Djankov et al. 2003; Kornai 1986; Megginson and Netter 2001; Aghion et al. 2005; Bruhn 2011
